facts.statement: Mopsitta tanta is an extinct bird found in the Early Eocene of Denmark.
facts.quote: Mopsitta tanta is an extinct bird of uncertain taxonomic position from the Early Eocene of Denmark

facts.statement: The remains of Mopsitta tanta were recovered from the Fur Formation.
facts.quote: its remains were recovered from the Fur Formation

facts.statement: The only known specimen of Mopsitta tanta is a single humerus bone of large size.
facts.quote: So far, the holotype and only known specimen is a single humerus bone of rather large size

facts.statement: Researchers initially thought Mopsitta tanta might be the oldest known crown-group parrot because it resembled Recent Psittacidae.
facts.quote: it was initially presumed to be phylogenetically closer to Recent Psittacidae than to other known Palaeogene psittaciforms and may, therefore, represent the oldest known crown-group parrot

facts.statement: Further examination revealed that the fossil lacks clear features defining it as a psittaciform or psittacid.
facts.quote: However, further examination subsequently pointed out that the fossil lacks clear psittaciform (let alone psittacid) apomorphies

facts.statement: It is debated whether the humerus belongs to Mopsitta tanta or the ibis genus Rhynchaeites, as it matches Rhynchaeites better except for size.
facts.quote: it was hypothesized that the M. tanta humerus actually belongs in that genus, being a better match (except in size) to the known Rhynchaeites remains than to any psittaciform fossil hitherto found

facts.statement: The species is nicknamed the "Danish Blue Parrot" or "Norwegian Blue" after a Monty Python sketch.
facts.quote: The species has been nicknamed the "Danish Blue Parrot", or the "Norwegian Blue", in honor of the Dead Parrot sketch from Monty Python's Flying Circus

facts.statement: Mopsitta is classified within the parent group Psittaciformes.
Mopsitta lived during the Ypresian stage, between 56 and 48.07 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Ypresian to Ypresian (56 to 48.07 million years ago)
